title: Xをしたい vs Xがしたい
summary: Both are fine: が says that X is making you want it; を says that you want to do the action.

blocks.text: The adjective of desire たい points at something. In **パンが食べたい**, it points at the bread: "the bread is want-inducing (to me)". But you also hear **パンを食べたい**. Are the particles changing their meaning? No. They always mean the same thing; only the point of view changes.

rows: the bread is tempting me, right now
I want to do the action "eat bread"

blocks.text: パンが食べたい。 The bread makes me want to eat it.

cars.label: たい attaches to パンを食べ

blocks.text: パンを食べたい。 I want to eat bread. たい attaches to the whole unit パンを食べ, not to 食べ alone.
How can an adjective have an object? Because たい is attached to the whole unit パンを食べ, not to the verb 食べ alone. We can glue verbs and objects into one block and add たい to it.
Flipping polarity like this is normal, even in English: "We were happy that day" points at us, while "That was a happy day" points at the day.

blocks.en: I want to eat your pancreas. (the title of a famous novel, a real を + たい)

blocks.text: With food, drink and things you can see or feel, the thing pulls at you, so が fits.

blocks.jp: のどが渇いたから、水が飲みたい。
blocks.en: I'm thirsty, so I feel like having water. (the water tempts me)

blocks.text: When を is the natural choice

With abstract things or people, we do not feel the thing is "pulling" us. It is our own decision. It is also more respectful for people: 友達を助けたい, not 友達が助けたい, because the friend is not a tempting object.

blocks.en: I want to help my friend.
I want to protect my country.

blocks.jp: お腹がすいたから、早く食べたい。
blocks.en: I'm hungry, so I want to eat soon. (the adjective points back at me)

items: が + たい: the thing is the cause of the wish.
を + たい: I want to do that action; common with people and abstract things.
The particles never change meaning; the point of view does.

questions.instruction: What is the hidden main carriage in パンを食べたい?
questions.note: With を, たい points back at the speaker, the zero main carriage.

questions.instruction: Why can たい take を?
options: It attaches to the whole unit パンを食べ
questions.note: The verb and object become one block.

questions.instruction: Which pair says the same wish from two points of view?
options: パンが食べたい / パンを食べたい
パンが食べたい / パンが食べた
パンを食べたい / パンを食べない
パンに食べたい / パンで食べたい
questions.note: Same particles, different viewpoint.

questions.instruction: Which pair is a correct explanation?
options: が = the thing causes the wish; を = I want the action
が and を are always interchangeable by accent
questions.note: Same particles, different viewpoint.

questions.instruction: Fill the gap
questions.note: A person we want to protect does not tempt us like food: it is our own wish to do the action, so を.
questions.en: I want to protect my family.

questions.instruction: Which sentence fits best when the sight of a cake suddenly makes you want it?
questions.note: The cake is the thing pulling at you, so it is the main carriage with が.

questions.instruction: Build the sentence
questions.prompt: I want to help my mother.
questions.note: を + stem + たい: I want to do the action.
questions.en: I want to help my mother.

questions.instruction: Tap the word that たい points at
questions.note: The cake is the main carriage of たい.
questions.en: I want to eat cake today.

questions.instruction: Tap the word that たい points at
questions.note: 水が is the tempting thing, the main carriage of たい.
questions.en: It's hot, so I want some cold water right now.

questions.instruction: True or false?
questions.prompt: 母を手伝いたい。 The one who wants is a hidden "I" (zero pronoun).
questions.note: With を, たい points back at the speaker.
questions.en: I want to help my mother.

questions.instruction: Which particle points たい back at the speaker?
questions.note: With を, たい points back at the speaker.
questions.en: I want to watch a movie.

questions.instruction: Which particle shows the ramen is tempting you?
questions.note: が makes the ramen the main carriage of たい.

questions.instruction: What does が show in this sentence?
questions.prompt: 暑いから、冷たいジュースが飲みたい。
options: I have decided to sell juice
The cold juice is tempting me right now
I want to help the juice
questions.note: が makes the juice the thing that causes the wish.
questions.en: It's hot, so I want a cold juice.

questions.instruction: Why is this an odd way to say "I want to help my teacher"?
options: が makes the teacher a tempting thing, like food
が is only for the past
先生 cannot be a noun
助ける never takes たい
questions.note: For a person we use を: they are not an object that tempts us.
questions.en: I want to help my teacher.

questions.instruction: Fill the gap
questions.prompt: 困っている人＿助けたい。
questions.note: A person we want to help takes を.
questions.en: I want to help people in trouble.

questions.instruction: Fill the gap
questions.note: The object of the action you want to do takes を.
questions.en: I want to help my younger brother.

questions.instruction: True or false?
questions.prompt: 疲れたから、早く寝たい。 No tempting thing appears, so たい points back at the speaker.
questions.note: Nothing pulls at me; I want to do the action.
questions.en: I'm tired, so I want to go to bed soon.

questions.instruction: Build the sentence
questions.prompt: I feel like watching a movie today.
questions.note: The topic comes first, then the main carriage 映画が, then the engine.
questions.en: I feel like watching a movie today.

questions.instruction: Why does 先生を助けたい use を?
options: Because 先生 is a place
Because を is the past tense
Because helping a person is our own wish to act, not a pull from a thing
Because たい cannot take が
questions.note: People are not tempting objects: we want to do the action.

questions.instruction: In 水が飲みたい, which word is the main carriage?
questions.note: The water makes me want to drink.

questions.instruction: Which sentence is wrong?
questions.note: に cannot mark what you drink: が or を.

questions.instruction: Build the sentence
questions.prompt: I want to help my grandmother.
questions.note: を + stem + たい: I want to do the action.
questions.en: I want to help my grandmother.
